I haven't implemented `title(text)`, because the tests contradict the spec.

- `test_words` is consistent with it: `'hello world'` → `'Hello World'`.
- `test_three` expects `title('one two three')` to return `'One two Three'`. That leaves the middle word lowercase, which conflicts with "capitalise the first letter of every word". The spec would give `'One Two Three'`.

No sensible rule satisfies both the spec and that test. Passing it would need a hack, such as capitalising only odd-positioned words, or special-casing the input. That would be working around the tests, so I stopped.

Please confirm which is right. If the spec is correct, `test_three` should expect `'One Two Three'`. If the test is correct, the spec needs to describe the rule it actually wants. The spec-faithful version is `' '.join(w[:1].upper() + w[1:].lower() for w in text.split(' '))`.
